From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated capacity planning request - ACME Q3 commitments

Priya / ACME procurement team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, ACME is planning to convert the POC into a Reserved Dedicated pool for Q3. You indicated an initial commit of ~75k token-hours/day which maps roughly to a 6-GPU dedicated pool under our baseline latency targets (p50 120ms for inference). We need a signed SOW + payment milestone to lock that capacity in our Dedicated pool.

Quick asks from our side so we can schedule the reservation:
- Confirm final committed token-hours/day and start date (you mentioned early July).
- Any hard SLA windows (e.g., 99.9% p99 latency during 9a–6p PT) or blackout dates.
- Point of contact for billing/procurement (added purchasing@acme.ai)

Heads-up: we currently have an overlapping high-visibility trial from OrbitAI scheduled in that same week that requests burst access to a shared GPU cluster. OrbitAI has not purchased reserved capacity; they are in an accelerated trial and have asked for temporary higher concurrency for demo runs.

Given this overlap, I want to get alignment internally on prioritization rules before we commit. Marissa / Karthik — can you confirm the process for allocating Dedicated GPUs when two customers contend and one has a reserved contract in-flight? I suspect the right move is to honor the committed reservation (once SOW is signed) and offer OrbitAI a preemptible burst with credits, but want to surface any operational constraints (migration windows, node pinning, quota changes).

I'll attach the SOW draft we shared and a short matrix of potential allocation options.

Best,
Jordan Blake

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-04T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning request - ACME Q3 commitments

Jordan / Karthik —

I'm attaching a short note (Q3-Capacity-Impact-Notes.txt) and a worked spreadsheet that shows three allocation policies:

1) Strict reservation-first: signed Reserved capacity > anything else. Preempt trials and bursts. (Pros: predictable billing, meets SLAs. Cons: temporary utilization dips if reserved pool underused.)

2) Revenue-weighted share: allocate by committed ARR + short-term expected usage. Useful when multiple signed deals but limited hardware. (Pros: balances business impact. Cons: complex arbitration, requires up-to-date ARR mapping.)

3) Soft-reservation with burst windows: reserve baseline for committed customers, allow short scheduled burst windows for trials (pre-scheduled & billed). (Pros: flexibility; Cons: operational overhead.)

For ACME specifically, their SOW and requested SLA strongly point to policy #1 once the SOW is signed and payment milestone is processed. If Jordan can get the signed SOW and initial invoice cleared by 6/20, we can lock their pool into Dedicated and provision GPUs (6xA100-equivalent) by 7/02.

For OrbitAI, we should offer a scheduled 4-hour demo window on preemptible nodes with a 20% service credit if they are preempted. That keeps OrbitAI moving without compromising production reservations.

Let me know if you want me to draft the customer-facing email templates for either outcome.

-Marissa
Sr. Manager, Capacity Ops
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: Q3-Capacity-Impact-Notes.txt, GPU_Retention_Options.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-07T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity planning request - request for arbitration

Sean — forwarding the thread. TL;DR: ACME intends to convert to Reserved (75k token-hours/day) and expects Dedicated GPUs in early July. OrbitAI requests temporary burst access during demo week (not reserved).

Impact analysis (quick):
- If we honor ACME reservation (policy #1), we commit ~6 GPUs for the month of July. That consumes ~18% of our US-west Dedicated A100 pool during peak.
- If we instead split and give OrbitAI a portion, we risk missing ACME SLA or having to offer credits if we preempt them later.

Options to arbitrate:
A) Prioritize ACME (recommendation) — requires sign + payment by 6/20. Notify OrbitAI and schedule demo on preemptible cluster.
B) Split 50/50 for July — requires an executive waiver and pro-rated discounts on both deals. Operationally messy for routing and monitoring.
C) Move ACME to a pinned physical node and isolate OrbitAI to autoscaled shared nodes — viable but provisioning lead time is +2 weeks, pushes start to 7/16.

We need a decision for Jordan to communicate to ACME and OrbitAI by EOD 6/09 to meet provisioning timelines. Please advise.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Dedicated Product Operations
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-09T11:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning request - decision and next steps

Team —

Thanks for the clear options. After weighing revenue predictability, SLA obligations, and operational risk, we will:

1) Prioritize ACME under Strict reservation-first policy. Once Jordan confirms signed SOW and initial invoice cleared by 2026-06-20, Capacity Ops will pin a 6-GPU block and mark it as Reserved in the scheduler by 2026-07-02.

2) Offer OrbitAI a 4-hour scheduled demo window on preemptible nodes the week of 7/06 with a 20% service credit if preempted. We will also offer a 30-day trial extension (no reserved capacity) and a 10% discount on first-month committed capacity if they choose to convert.

3) Jordan: please send ACME a brief confirmation email with deadlines (SOW sign + payment by 6/20) and copy Procurement on the invoice routing. Marissa / Karthik: please prepare the provisioning ticket for pinning and the customer-facing templates. I expect a follow-up status update in 48 hours.

If any customer pushes back on credits or contractual terms, escalate to me immediately.

-S
Sean Gallagher
VP, Sales Operations
